From a distance: A cool pale blue-grey granular finish with frosty sparkle; it reads like crushed ice or granite, light and cold. Measured spec (average): metal 71, roughness 43, coat 49. articles.summary: Olive-khaki with a fine woven cross-cut grain, like shredded paper or burlap; muted gold-green, semi-matte. A muted khaki-olive car with a coarse horizontal weave; strip rows merge into a canvas or burlap texture.
articles.what: Security-grade shredding: 2mm strips, cross-cut, unreconstructable and oddly beautiful. Up close: Olive-khaki and mustard strips about 6 px tall and 8-16 px long, wobbling in horizontal courses like shredded paper or woven straw, with dark brown gaps between the rows. Fine vertical tick lines cut across each strip for the cross-cut look. From a distance: A muted khaki-olive car with a coarse horizontal weave; strip rows merge into a canvas or burlap texture. Measured spec (average): metal 112, roughness 124, coat 118. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.

Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body sides and hood: horizontal courses follow the car length
Roof: wide area shows the strip rows
Black or white numbers read; khaki or olive numbers vanish into the weave.
Black or white stripes and bands: clean contrast on the earth tone
Pairs well with: black, white, brown, orange.
pitfalls: Not a woven cloth grid: strips run only in horizontal wavy courses
Not bright gold: it is dull khaki and olive
Avoid: muddy under yellow or green numbers, flat lighting kills the weave.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 112 (pearl-level metal), roughness 124 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 118 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: muddy under yellow or green numbers, flat lighting kills the weave.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: black or white stripes and bands: clean contrast on the earth tone; big graphics and number plates: weave is calm enough at distance
Patterns to avoid: fine line, weave or carbon patterns: they fight the strip rows; camo: it buries the cross-cut texture
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat gradient: adds contrast to the dry strips; soft metallic patches: adds depth without grain
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.summary: Dusty rose-red with a strong horizontal brick weave, satin finish and a faint holographic shimmer. Reads as a dusty rose-copper car with a strongly striped brick texture; the bars stay visible as horizontal banding, the colour is a warm salmon-brown.
